sections.title: How ATHA serves education and research
sections.text: ATHA creates a living laboratory where HADORA’s principles are tested in real, ambitious work. It shows whether a human-centred culture can lead to stronger decisions, deeper collaboration, and exceptional outcomes without exhaustion. Learning from each experience refines both the ATHA methodology and the HADORA approach. It also bridges education and industry, connecting students, alumni, faculty, and researchers with real challenges so talent and theory meet practice in meaningful ways.

sections.title: Warwick Business School's role in ATHA
sections.text: Warwick Business School provides the academic partnership, credibility, community, and physical setting for ATHA. While OneMundi owns the purpose and delivery, and HADORA shapes the human experience, Warwick Business School brings essential academic depth and connection. Its deeper interest lies in understanding how people should be educated for the AI-native era — combining technical, human, and ethical capacities to shape future changemakers.

sections.title: What ATHA really is
sections.text: ATHA envisions a world where AI-native innovation creates extraordinary business and societal value while making work healthier, more joyful, more responsible, and more human. It brings together education, research, industry, talent, experience design, and AI-native transformation to solve real-world challenges. sections.title: Why ATHA exists — what makes it different
sections.text: ATHA exists to create and operate AI-native innovation experiences and a global ecosystem where people and organizations can work on real industry challenges. It helps them understand AI holistically, make better decisions about its use, and experience healthier, more human ways of working. sections.title: What ATHA brings together
sections.text: As currently planned, ATHA connects participants who are normally separated: education, research, and industry. It brings together students, alumni, educators, and institutions developing AI-native changemaker capabilities. Research centers and academic partners help study, challenge, measure, and strengthen the methodology. Organizations contribute real challenges, commercial context, and implementation opportunities — creating a bridge between theory and practice.

sections.title: OneMundi builds and operates ATHA
sections.text: As currently planned, OneMundi carries the main responsibility for making ATHA real. It develops the concept, activates stakeholders, and connects Warwick Business School, HADORA, research centers, industry partners, students, alumni, and other participants. OneMundi also attracts challenges and partners, builds traction and participation, and develops the ecosystem that sustains ATHA between editions.

sections.title: The current state of the first ATHA edition
sections.text: As currently planned, the first ATHA edition will involve around 45 selected participants, centred at Warwick Business School. Nine multidisciplinary teams of five will work on three real enterprise AI challenges, with three independent teams addressing each challenge. The core working location will be Warwick/Coventry, featuring a multi-day experience at Warwick Business School. sections.title: The arc every ATHA edition follows
sections.text: Each ATHA edition follows a thoughtful arc: participants arrive and are met rather than processed, as the room is made with care. They open the sense of the question before attacking it, seeing it as it truly sits. Teams then form across disciplines around the question. The longest stage is creation — where AI-native investigation unfolds, AI is used fully but never accepted blindly.
